facts.statement: Rugops had an estimated length of 4.4 to 5.3 meters and a weight of 410 kilograms.
facts.quote: Rugops has an estimated length of 4.4 - 5.3 m and weight of 410 kg

facts.statement: The top of Rugops' skull had pits correlating with scales, and its snout likely had an armour-like dermis.
facts.quote: The top of its skull bears several pits which correlates with overlaying scale and the front of the snout would have had an armour-like dermis

facts.statement: Rugops primus was described in 2004 by Paul Sereno, Jeffrey Wilson, and Jack Conrad based on a partial skull.
facts.quote: In 2004, this skull was described by American researchers Paul Sereno, Jeffrey Wilson, and Jack Conrad as the holotype (name-bearing) specimen of a new genus and species of abelisaurid, named Rugops primus

facts.statement: The skull of Rugops measured approximately 31.5 centimeters in length.
facts.quote: The skull length of Rugops was about 31.5 cm

facts.statement: Rugops possesses two unique derived characters (autapomorphies) distinguishing it from other dinosaurs.
facts.quote: The describing authors indicated two distinguishing traits. Both of these are autapomorphies, unique derived characters

facts.statement: Researchers suggested that depressions on Rugops' nasal bones anchored sensory structures or soft tissues for display.
facts.quote: Sereno et al. (2004) suggested that the depressions on the dorsal surface of each nasal anchored either sensory structures or soft tissues for display

facts.statement: Delcourt (2018) interpreted the nasal depressions as correlating with overlying scales similar to those of crocodiles and lizards.
facts.quote: Delcourt (2018), however, interpreted that they correlate with overlying scales, as seen in extant reptiles such as crocodiles and lizards

facts.statement: Delcourt (2018) proposed that Rugops' armour-like dermis may have been used for low-motion headbutting behavior.
facts.quote: Delcourt (2018) also proposed that the armour-like dermis may correlate with a low-motion headbutting behaviour, as seen in marine iguanas

facts.statement: Multiple analyses have recovered Rugops as the most basal abelisaurid.
facts.quote: Sereno et al. (2004) initially found Rugops to be the basalmost abelisaurid, a position also recovered by various analyses by Egli et al. (2016), Delcourt (2018), Cerroni et al. (2020) and Rolando et al. (2020)

facts.statement: Some studies place Rugops as more derived than Rahiolisaurus and Eoabelisaurus but more basal than other abelisaurids.
facts.quote: However, Rugops has also been recovered as being more derived than Rahiolisaurus and/or Eoabelisaurus but more basal than other abelisaurids by Pol & Rauhut (2012), Rauhut & Carrano (2016), and Iori et al. (2021)

facts.statement: The Echkar Formation where Rugops fossils were found dates to around 96 million years ago.
facts.quote: These layers belong to the Echkar Formation, which dates to the Cenomanian age of the Late Cretaceous period, around 96 million years ago

facts.statement: Rugops lived in a fluvial and lacustrine environment with humid or semi-arid conditions.
facts.quote: The Echkar Formation is a fluvial and lacustrine deposit which occurred in a humid or semi-arid conditions

facts.statement: Rugops lived alongside theropods like Carcharodontosaurus iguidensis and Spinosaurus.
facts.quote: Rugops lived alongside several other dinosaurs. These included other theropods, such as the carcharodontosaurid Carcharodontosaurus iguidensis (which may be from another genus) and the spinosaurid Spinosaurus

facts.statement: Rugops is classified within the family Abelisauridae.
facts.quote: familia: Abelisauridae

facts.statement: Rugops is known from a partial skull found in the Echkar Formation and a left maxilla from the Kem Kem Beds, with an initial estimated length of 6 meters and weight of 750 kilograms.
facts.quote: Aunque se conoce solo por un cráneo parcial encontrado en la Formación Echkar y un maxilar izquierdo de los Lechos de Kem Kem, se estimó inicialmente que Rugops tenía 6 metros de largo y 750 kilogramos de peso según las comparaciones con sus parientes.

facts.statement: Later estimates revised the length of Rugops to 4.4 meters.
facts.quote: Estimaciones posteriores sugieren una longitud revisada de 4,4 metros.

facts.statement: Other authors suggest Rugops measured 5.3 meters in length and weighed 410 kilograms.
facts.quote: Al mismo tiempo, otros autores sugieren que medía 5,3 metros de largo y 410 kilogramos de peso.

facts.statement: The skull length of Rugops was approximately 31.5 centimeters.
facts.quote: La longitud del cráneo de Rugops era de unos 31,5 centímetros.

facts.statement: Paul Sereno suggested that Rugops may have been a scavenger because its head was not designed for fighting or crushing bones.
facts.quote: Paul Sereno, quien dirigió el equipo que descubrió el fósil, dijo que "no es el tipo de cabeza diseñada para pelear o aplastar huesos", sugiriendo que pudo haber sido un carroñero.

facts.statement: The top of the Rugops skull has two rows of seven holes with unknown purposes, though Sereno speculated they may have anchored a display crest or horns based on blood vessel grooves leading to them.
facts.quote: La parte superior del cráneo tiene dos filas de siete agujeros, cada uno con un propósito desconocido, aunque Sereno ha especulado que pueden haber anclado algún tipo de cresta de exhibición o cuernos, basado en la presencia de surcos para los vasos sanguíneos que forman un camino hacia estos hoyos.

facts.statement: Like other abelisaurids, Rugops likely had very short or even vestigial arms.
facts.quote: Al igual que otros abelisáuridos, Rugops probablemente tenía brazos muy cortos o incluso vestigiales.

facts.statement: The Rugops skull was discovered in 2000 by Paul Sereno in the Echkar Formation of the Sahara Desert in Niger.
facts.quote: El cráneo de Rugops fue descubierto en 2000 por Paul Sereno, en la Formación Echkar del desierto del Sahara de Níger.

facts.statement: The discovery of the Rugops skull in Niger in 2000 was crucial for understanding theropod evolution in the area and proved that the landmass was still connected to Gondwana at that time.
facts.quote: El descubrimiento del cráneo de Rugops en Níger en 2000 fue un avance crucial en la comprensión de la evolución de los terópodos en esa área y demuestra que esta masa de tierra todavía estaba unida con Gondwana en esa etapa de la historia.

facts.statement: Rugops lived in the same location and geological time period as Spinosaurus, Carcharodontosaurus, and Deltadromeus.
facts.quote: Vivió en la misma localidad y período de tiempo geológico que Spinosaurus, Carcharodontosaurus y Deltadromeus.

facts.statement: The type species Rugops primus means 'first wrinkled face' and is thought to be phylogenetically related to Majungasaurus.
facts.quote: El nombre de la especie tipo, Rugops primus, significa «primera cara arrugada» y se piensa que es una especie filogenéticamente relacionada con Majungasaurus.

facts.statement: Rugops is considered a basal representative of Abelisauridae.
facts.quote: Se considera que Rugops es un representante básico de Abelisauridae.

facts.statement: Rugops does not belong to Brachyrostra, South American abelisaurids, or the Majungasaurinae of India, Madagascar, and Europe, but is a separate genus similar to Kryptops.
facts.quote: Este no pertenece ni a Brachyrostra, los abeliáuridos sudaméricanos ni a Majungasaurinae de la India, Madagascar y Europa, con los que se pensaría que estaría más relacionado, sino que es un género aparte, al igual que Kryptops.

facts.statement: Rugops lived during the Cenomanian stage, from 100.5 to 93.9 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Cenomanian to Cenomanian (100.5 to 93.9 million years ago)

facts.statement: The parent group of Rugops is Abelisauridae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Abelisauridae

facts.statement: The type species of the genus Rugops is Rugops primus.
facts.quote: Type species: Rugops primus
